chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“The leftover water of the pigeon and the chicken—there is no harm in it—and [that of] birds.” His statement, “and birds,” is general regarding every bird.

key_terms.الدَّجَاجِ: chicken or fowl, mentioned as an example in the ruling
key_terms.الْحَمَامَةِ: the pigeon or dove, mentioned as an example in the ruling
key_terms.فَضْلُ: leftover water or remaining liquid after an animal has drunk from it
key_terms.كُلِّ طَيْرٍ: every bird without exception in the wording
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no problem or objection in it; it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is the leftover water of pigeons, chickens, and other birds permissible to use for purification?
ai.summary: This report gives a legal ruling that the leftover water associated with pigeons, chickens, and birds is not problematic. The wording indicates a general application to all birds, making it relevant to rulings of taharah (ritual purity) and what may be used for purification.
